paragraphs.text: Meaning, the inhabitants of Samaria, whom the king of Assyria had placed in the place of the ten tribes, 2Ki 17:24,19:37. They professed God but worshipped idols and therefore were the greatest enemies to the true servants of God.
paragraphs.label: a
paragraphs.anchor: the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin

paragraphs.text: For they knew their pretence, that is to erect idolatry instead of true religion.
paragraphs.label: b
paragraphs.anchor: but we ourselves together will build

paragraphs.text: They bribed the governors under the king to hinder their work, thus they that hinder cannot understand that God would be purely served.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: Called Artaxerxes, which signifies in the Persian tongue an excellent warrior.

paragraphs.text: These were people whom the Assyrians placed in Samaria instead of the ten tribes.

paragraphs.text: Some think it was not Sennacherib, but rather Salmanasar.

paragraphs.text: That is, Euphrates, and he means in respect to Babel that they dwelt beyond it.
